A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same causal graph cut study and include Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to first-page publication information and one bibliography entry with associated reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and ridesharing-simulator results in Section 4, plus regression and data-use ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original synthetic experiments, ridesharing-simulator results, and appendix ablations, including Figures 5–9.

M1.justification: The surrogate objective, spectral graph cut procedure, iterative covariance estimation, and ATE estimators are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 and the general-cluster formulation in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic spatial layouts, three covariance structures, 85-region ridesharing simulator, and single-experiment scenarios.

E2.justification: SC, TNET, CC, GD, ID, and OCGC retain identical participation in the corresponding comparisons. The simulator still excludes OCGC, and the single-experiment comparison still excludes GD.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report identical outcome models, parameter ranges, relative-MSE evaluation, simulator settings, and data-processing and estimation procedures.

E4.justification: The covariance-noise robustness analysis in Figure 7 and the pooled-versus-local regression and cumulative-versus-current-batch data ablations in Figures 8–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: The reported 50 independent synthetic replications, Monte Carlo procedure for approximating the simulator's true ATE, and confidence-interval displays are unchanged. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All plotted and stated results match, including the synthetic and simulator comparisons, covariance-noise findings, and appendix ablations. Figures 3 and 5–9 retain identical result entries and trends.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 1, Propositions 1–4, the general-cluster surrogate in Appendix A, and all proofs in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same claims about accommodating moderate-to-large interference, adapting to covariance structure, computational efficiency, and improved ATE estimation.

C2.justification: The interpretation of interference and correlation as opposing design forces is unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning omitted second-order interference and applicability beyond independently repeated experiments.

D1.justification: The Python implementation link and technical disclosures are identical, including simulator construction, random-forest outcome regression, cross-fitting, spatial feature augmentation, and accumulated-data fitting in Appendix C.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The Zhou et al. (2025) reference expands IS and OPE in its title but identifies the same work; this is a bibliographic wording update.

P1.justification: The proceedings footer changes from the 41st to the 42nd conference, the arXiv version/date stamp updates, and one reference title expands its abbreviations. The main narrative, section organization, and appendices otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: The expanded Zhou et al. reference causes limited line wrapping and shifts subsequent bibliography entries on page 14. All scientific figures, algorithm displays, equations, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication information and expands one bibliographic title, with slight local reflow. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations—including the appendices—are identical. These small editorial updates do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
